It investigates whether a deliberately unoccupied six-module mobile-city research system can reduce relocation-related material loss through qualified reuse, automated selective disassembly and auditable remanufacturing, while preserving deployment latency and critical-service safety. The three-way research coupling is Circular Materials x Autonomous Manufacturing x Urban Sustainability. Neither a functioning autonomous city nor a human-occupied habitat is asserted. The falsifiable proposal compares a frozen circular material strategy against competent conventional manual recovery, replacement and stationary emergency infrastructure under equal material, energy, sensing, technician-hour, tool, water and transport budgets. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. Thirty mechanism-distinct research formula plates address mass custody, qualified yield, bond separation work, fatigue, polymer rheology, sensor residuals, covariance, electrical energy, verified lifecycle inventory, carbon-allocation sensitivity, replacement counterfactuals, tail risk, second-site reproduction and noncompensatory physical release. The original contract's cyber-physical residual r_k = y_k - yhat_k(x_k,u_k) is retained as one fault-detection method; it is not treated as a law of circularity or sustainability. Every mathematical plate states units, validity assumptions, a blinded counterexample and scientific chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated research studies and 200 Research Gates, each connected to a specified material state, independent reference, fault or competing process. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose research instruments, material-qualification fixtures, provenance devices, circularity accounting tools and successor-ready evidence protocols. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. Its complete PDF also contains research limits, negative-result custody and second-laboratory transfer requirements. The scope remains prospective, scaled and non-occupancy. Environmental performance requires functional-unit parity and a complete lifecycle inventory; increasing recovered mass alone does not prove lower environmental burden. items.summary: This Python software provides a Docker-based workflow for electroencephalography (EEG) quality control, preprocessing and feature extraction . It supports reproducible research on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents using the task recordings in the BALLADEER dataset. The software documents and implements the processing workflow underlying A task EEG dataset with preprocessed signals and features for ADHD research in children and adolescents . That companion resource contains 669 eligible recordings from 156 participants and 115 feature definitions or templates across seven feature families. The recordings and generated feature tables are distributed separately from this software. What the software does Raw EEG quality assessment: characterizes recording quality before preprocessing and produces structured quality summaries. Recording eligibility and correction plans: applies the supplied, frozen label-blind selection records, including recording eligibility and approved channel-interpolation actions. Conservative EEG preprocessing: processes continuous blocks without bridging acquisition gaps, applies 0.5–40 Hz filtering, harmonizes sampling to 128 Hz, and performs conditional channel interpolation and average referencing. Post-preprocessing quality assessment: calculates quality summaries and comparisons with the original recordings. EEG feature extraction: generates seven feature families using aligned, gap-aware windows of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds with 50% overlap, subject to each estimator's duration requirements. Output verification: checks processing lineage, cross-stage consistency and recorded checksums. The supplied selection records preserve the decisions used for the companion dataset. Reusing those records does not repeat the original manual review or establish new eligibility decisions for another cohort. Seven EEG feature families Temporal and statistical features. Conventional spectral features. Aperiodic spectral features. Complexity and fractal features. Functional connectivity features. Graph and network features. Time-frequency decomposition features. Feature definitions expand across channels, channel pairs and other indexed positions. Outputs retain calculation states and reasons for unavailable or undefined values. Duration-dependent support is explicit; for example, the configured aperiodic spectral analysis uses 8- and 16-second windows. Supported recordings, inputs and outputs The input is the original BALLADEER dataset, version 2 , obtained from its version-specific Figshare record . Extract the source data before running the software. Set --input-dir to the directory that directly contains users_demographics.json and participant directories such as UB0004/ , preserving the original task subdirectories and filenames. The companion Zenodo derivative dataset is an output resource, not the input to this complete reproduction workflow. The packaged workflow is configured for five BALLADEER task conditions: CogniFit cognitive assessment, Attention Robots, and Slackline levels 1, 6 and 11. Users also provide a writable output directory. The input directory is mounted read-only. Outputs include preprocessed EEG signals in MNE-FIF format, tabular feature outputs, quality summaries, calculation-state records, configuration snapshots, processing manifests and checksums. The software archive includes label-blind selection metadata with pseudonymous recording identifiers; it does not contain the original EEG recordings or the generated derivative dataset. Reproducibility and package contents The archive includes Python source code, scientific configurations, a Dockerfile, version-pinned Python dependencies, shell launchers, validation tests and documentation. Users can run individual processing stages, extract one feature family for one task, or execute the complete sequential workflow. Graph features use the corresponding connectivity outputs. items.summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .
items.title: DinHot: A Holographic Optical Trap Studio Comparing Hologram Methods on a Device Model

items.summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol

items.summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

items.summary: Enterprise email security protects employees behind a corporate mail gateway. The people most exposed to employment and support-impersonation scams - students and early-career job seekers - are contacted inside consumer platforms, where no gateway sees the message. We present a dependency-free, explainable detector that works at the level of the individual message and its sender, and a public benchmark for comparing such detectors under cheap adversarial transformation. The detector has four layers: (1) deterministic lookalike checks built on Unicode UTS #39 confusable skeletons, mixed-script detection, bounded edit distance, and brand-agnostic detection of a domain hidden inside a link host; (2) a logistic-regression sender scorer over 23 named features trained on a synthetic generator spanning eight brands (holdout F1 0.987); (3) a message-intent classifier, with a rule baseline and a prompt-injection-hardened LLM wrapper, that receives structured sender facts from the first two layers and whose impersonation verdicts are discounted deterministically only when the sender is verified or unremarkable, nothing sensitive is asked, links stay under the sender's control, and the body does not claim the platform's authority; and (4) a 76-message, brand-parametric benchmark with ten label-preserving adversarial variants and three model-paraphrased corpora, scored on per-layer recall, false-positive rate, injection hijack rate, and latency. On a paraphrased corpus frozen before a single evaluation, all three Layer 3 backends reach recall 1.00 in the fused pipeline, at FPR 0.03 for the rule baseline and Gemma 3 27B and 0.10 for Llama 3.1 8B, against 0.83/0.03, 1.00/0.07 and 1.00/0.47 for the same backends unfused: the sender layers are worth 17 points of recall to the rules and 37 points of FPR to the small model. The 8B model obeyed an appended injection on 6 of 46 attacks, each caught only by a deterministic overrule; the 27B model obeyed none. Three findings fall out: UTS #39 skeletons do not fold Cyrillic U+0442 or Greek U+03BA to ASCII, so skeleton equality alone misses a mixed-script brand lookalike; regex intent cues lose 33 points of recall to a single confusable glyph unless text is confusable-folded first; and negation must be handled at clause level with an exception for conditionals. Code, weights, corpora, and per-message verdict dumps are released under the MIT license.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement.
